The visualization combines grouped bar charts and a line graph to convey trade balance values in billion USD on the left vertical axis and GDP growth percentages on the right vertical axis. The countries are listed along the horizontal axis, including the Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Greece, and Poland. The trade balance data is represented through three sets of vertical bars for each country, color-coded to distinguish the years: blue for 2020, red for 2021, and green for 2022. The Netherlands consistently exhibits the highest trade surpluses, with values slightly decreasing over the three years, from approximately 22.5 billion USD in 2020 to 19.8 billion USD in 2022. Germany follows a similar trend, showing strong surpluses that decline from around 18.7 billion USD in 2020 to 15.2 billion USD in 2022. Belgium maintains a moderate surplus, though its values also show a slight decrease from 5.1 billion USD to 4.7 billion USD over the same period. France, displaying a marginal surplus, shows a decline from 4.8 billion USD in 2020 to 1.5 billion USD in 2022. Italy transitions from a small deficit of 2.3 billion USD in 2020 to a larger deficit of 5.6 billion USD by 2022. Spain, Portugal, and Greece exhibit trade deficits, with Spain’s deficit growing from 10.2 billion USD in 2020 to 14.3 billion USD in 2022, Portugal’s from 8.9 billion USD to 10.5 billion USD, and Greece’s from 15.6 billion USD to 18.9 billion USD. Poland’s trade deficit slightly increases from 3.4 billion USD in 2020 to 4.2 billion USD in 2022. Overlaying this bar chart, a purple line graph depicts the 2022 GDP growth percentages for each country. Portugal leads with a notable growth rate of 6.7%, followed by Greece at 5.9%, and Spain at 5.5%. Poland and the Netherlands also show strong growth at 4.9% and 4.5%, respectively. Italy and Belgium exhibit moderate growth rates of 3.7% and 3.0%, while France and Germany demonstrate lower growth at 2.5% and 1.8%, respectively. The chart effectively highlights the contrast between trade balances and economic growth, revealing that countries with larger deficits do not necessarily correlate with lower GDP growth rates.

**One side effect, fixed this turn:** switching the 2020 trace to Bar made its hover text (Trade_Stage) draw inside the bars. Some of it is tiny and unreadable. On the old Scatter trace this text only appeared on hover, so I'm adding textposition='none' to keep it hover-only. Nothing else changes.
